thread:
incident-bot: PAGER: Smart-routing fallback spike detected. Multiple routed requests to 'variant:v2-quant' are failing with 502/timeout after region fallback; latency >5s for served reps. Affects hosted->dedicated spillover path. Auto-suppress threshold tripped at 2755551200.

nicole (oncall): I'm oncall and see the alert, acknowledging. Paging shawn and alex-sre.

shawn (eng): I'm awake, pulling logs. Initial look: routing policy 'smart-fallback-v3' started sending traffic to eu-west fallback, but the routing map flagged v2-quant as incompatible, so it re-routed into Dedicated pools that don't have that quantized kernel compiled — resulted in hot-path errors.

marc (ml): That matches model-variant mismatch. Dedicated pools are running a non-quantized build (float32 kernels only). If the policy falls back to a variant that's not actually deployed on the target pool, we get adapter errors -> 502.

eva (support): Customer impact: two tenants reported elevated errors (tenant-alpha, tenant-beta). Support tickets opened, some users saw generation stops. ETA on mitigation?

shawn (eng): Immediate plan: 1) disable the 'smart-fallback-v3' routing rule to stop cross-tier spillover, 2) force-route new requests to hosted catalog variant 'v2-quant-hosted' until we confirm dedicated has compatible kernels. Doing step 1 now.

shawn (eng): Executing CLI to patch policy:
```bash
redwoodctl routing update --policy smart-fallback-v3 --enabled false --reason "Emerg: misvariant -> spillover errors"
```

incident-bot: ACTION: Policy smart-fallback-v3 disabled by shawn at 2755551228. Re-routing to fallback policy 'hosted-only' for affected tiers.

nicole (oncall): Observability: increasing from 0.2% to 5.6% 502s pre-patch. Post-disable: watching metrics. Alex, can you increase dedicated pool eviction cooldown so we don't thrash?

alex-sre: On it — bumping eviction cooldown + temporarily blocking automatic pool-claim from hosted.

shawn (eng): Posting a quick grep of error traces:
```
2026-03-15T02:20:11Z ERROR shard=ded-03 handler=serving.go: runtime error: backend kernel 'quant_kern_v2' not found
```

marc (ml): Root cause hypothesis: a config push from an onboarding script changed the variant alias mapping (regex for "quant" variants) to include v2-quant in the fallback set. It matched earlier than intended so the routing stack preferred that path. Need to audit last week of variant mapping changes.

lina (product): Drafting customer-facing blurb for status page and sentries. Short note: "We experienced a routing policy misconfiguration causing some requests to be routed to incompatible dedicated pools resulting in errors and higher latency. Impacted customers: tenant-alpha, tenant-beta. Mitigation in progress." I'll post after wording review. @eva - can you confirm affected accounts list?

eva (support): Confirmed tenant-alpha and tenant-beta. One additional partner integration (partner-x) had elevated latency but no hard errors.

nicole (oncall): From the oncall checklist: after disabling rule, if errors fall below 1% for 10m we consider this contained. If not, next step is force-swap to hosted variants + scale hosted capacity. Monitoring now.

incident-bot: METRIC: 502 rate fell to 0.9% at 2755551290 after disable. Latency median for affected buckets down to 480ms.

shawn (eng): Filling mitigation runbook:
- disabled offending routing policy
- blackholed eu-west fallback for tier 'default'
- temporarily forced hosted-only variant mapping
- started a compatibility audit for dedicated pool kernels

marc (ml): For long term: ensure variant->pool compatibility matrix enforced at routing decision time. If a variant isn't present in a target pool, route must skip that pool instead of sending and relying on errors.

lina (product): Status page draft pinned to incident channel: "Service degraded for some customers due to a routing configuration error. We're serving via hosted variants as a workaround. We're investigating and will update in 30 minutes." :hourglass_flowing_sand:

eva (support): Notifying affected tenants with current mitigation message.

nicole (oncall): Handing off to day shift: @shawn will continue with root cause and patch; alex-sre and marc will own the compatibility audit and kernel rollout plan. I'll add a follow-up incident ticket and move this to monitoring state once 20m stable.

shawn (eng): Quick follow-up: I found the exact config diff that introduced the alias expansion. Pushing a stricter match and adding a guard:
```yaml
routing_aliases:
  - name: quantized
    match: '^v[0-9]+-quant$'   # stricter, prevents v2-quant-legacy from matching
    allowed_pools: ['hosted','dedicated-quant-enabled']
```
Applying now.

incident-bot: CONFIG-CHANGE: routing_aliases updated by shawn at 2755551542. Canary applied to 10% of traffic.

marc (ml): Canary results look clean — no errors on canary. Proceeding to roll to 100% after 5m observation.

incident-bot: CANARY: 10% -> 100% at 2755551620, roll successful.

nicole (oncall): All clear threshold met: 30m stable, error rate under 0.5%. Containment confirmed.

lina (product): Updated status page with final note and ETA for postmortem: "Contained. Full postmortem to follow. We're scheduling a root-cause call for 11:00 UTC."

eva (support): Affected tenants notified with remediation steps and request for any lingering issues to be reported to support.

shawn (eng): Postmortem next actions: enforce compile-time checks for pool-kernel compatibility, add routing-time guard to skip incompatible pools, add e2e test for alias regex changes in CI.

nicole (oncall): Closing live incident thread. Handing off to SRE triage team for postmortem and RCA. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
